orders.writeAuthority: Order lifecycle RPCs / direct writes elsewhere in the app (out of this closure's scope to fully enumerate)
orders.projection: raw table read, filtered by status/department in various ways per consumer
orders.expectedSynchronisation: n/a (this is itself a source table)
flags: MISLABELLED_METRIC: productionQueueFeed.ts's `orders.status` pipeline count was surfaced under the bare label 'Production' in Live Work Queues, indistinguishable from the governed production_jobs count. FIXED this closure -- relabeled to 'Orders in Production Pipeline' and a separate 'Production Jobs (Governed)' KPI (src/hooks/useOpenProductionJobsCount.ts) now surfaces the production_jobs count under its own label.

production_jobs.writeAuthority: Governed RPCs only: accept_production_job, reject_production_job, start_production_job, pause_production_job, resume_production_job, advance_production_job_stage, record_production_output, declare_production_ready, dispatch_production_to_rgs, resolve_production_issue, report_production_issue, submit_production_day_end, quick_log_production_to_rgs (all in src/components/phh/*.tsx via rgsGovernedRpc) plus reserve_rgs_stock/create_production_shortage_demand from ReadyGoodsStore.tsx (job creation on shortage).
production_jobs.projection: raw table read filtered by canonical_department + status (OperationsController.tsx, FactoryTVModule.tsx)
production_jobs.expectedSynchronisation: canonical_department is trigger-maintained server-side in oasis-supabase-core -- client code treats it as authoritative and never derives it locally (per the typed-boundary comment added in commit f123418e).
flags: This is THE authoritative production authority. The golden regression case (SO#ABB4287E / OAS-RIN-3 / job E3ED28B0) lives here.

readers: DepartmentExecutionBoard.tsx (via useDepartmentExecutionBoard.ts -> operationalQueueReadStore.ts) for all seven execution/* boards
operational_queue_items.writeAuthority: NONE -- confirmed zero writers anywhere in oasis-supabase-core's migration history for every queue_type (owner-supplied finding, taken as given for this closure; this repo cannot inspect oasis-supabase-core directly).
operational_queue_items.projection: raw table read, filtered by queue_type per board
operational_queue_items.expectedSynchronisation: NONE POSSIBLE -- nothing ever writes to it
flags: DEAD_PROJECTION across all seven consumers. Three of the seven (execution/production, execution/assembly, execution/ready-goods) redirected to governed replacements this closure. The other four (execution/dispatch, execution/third-party, execution/retail, execution/complaints) and ExecutionCommandCenter.tsx are documented as LEGACY-SUPERSEDED SURFACE but left unredirected pending a confirmed 1:1 canonical replacement and a passing test, per the owner's explicit scope for this closure.

inventory_reservations.writeAuthority: Governed RPCs: reserve_rgs_stock, pick_rgs_reservation, issue_rgs_stock, release_rgs_reservation (all in ReadyGoodsStore.tsx via rgsGovernedRpc/callGovernedRpc)
inventory_reservations.projection: raw table read joined against orders/products per consumer
inventory_reservations.expectedSynchronisation: Reservation lifecycle fields (reserved_qty/fulfilled_qty/released_qty) are only ever mutated through the governed RPCs above -- no direct client writes found.

readers: ReadyGoodsStore.tsx (version read for optimistic concurrency on accept_rgs_production_receipt)
inventory_stock_balances.writeAuthority: Server-side only, via accept_rgs_production_receipt and issue_rgs_stock RPCs (balance mutation itself happens in oasis-supabase-core, not client code)
inventory_stock_balances.expectedSynchronisation: Client reads `version` before accept_rgs_production_receipt and passes p_expected_balance_version -- optimistic-concurrency guard against a stale balance read racing a concurrent acceptance.

production_rgs_transfers.projection: raw table read, joined to production_jobs by job_id for display
production_rgs_transfers.expectedSynchronisation: This table is the evidence trail between a production_jobs dispatch (dispatch_production_to_rgs) and RGS's physical receipt/acceptance -- rgs_notified flags whether the RGS side has acknowledged it yet.

rgs_issue_events.writeAuthority: Governed RPC: acknowledge_rgs_issue (and issue_rgs_stock creates the underlying issue event server-side)

commandCenterProductionKpi.defect: src/lib/live-feeds/productionQueueFeed.ts computed a count from legacy orders.status (via isProductionPipelineOrder), surfaced under the bare label 'Production' in src/pages/admin/LiveWorkQueues.tsx -- completely disconnected from the governed production_jobs authority.
commandCenterProductionKpi.fix: Option B implemented: (1) src/lib/work-queues/queueTypes.ts WORK_QUEUE_LABELS.production_queue relabeled 'Production' -> 'Orders in Production Pipeline'. (2) New src/lib/production-jobs/openProductionJobsCount.ts + src/hooks/useOpenProductionJobsCount.ts provide an authoritative open production_jobs count (statuses pending/accepted/in_production/paused). (3) LiveWorkQueues.tsx renders both as separate, distinctly labeled cards.
commandCenterProductionKpi.whyOptionB: A clean authoritative production_jobs count required new cross-cutting query wiring (a standalone hook, independent of the existing OperationalFeedContext/aggregateLiveFeeds pipeline, to avoid touching the WorkQueueId exhaustive-Record maps used by escalation/ownership/dependency projections) -- Option A (rewriting productionQueueFeed.ts itself to read production_jobs) would have changed what 'production_queue' items/pressure mean for every other consumer of aggregateLiveFeeds (queueEscalation.ts, queueOwnership.ts, cmdQueuePressure.ts), which was out of this closure's scope to fully re-verify.
